posts.content_md:
Regarding softening the existing emulsion, have you tried the old pre-toning emulsion softener? It was a standard for softening the emulsion of prints that had been fixed with a hardening fixer, so that they could be more easily toned and washed. The content was simple enough, 30 grams of sodium carbonate (monohydrate) and water to make a liter, with the print being immersed for up to ten minutes. I've never used it, so I can't vouch for any amount of softening or what it might do to film stock.

On the dye, since the price of five grams of the pinacyanol is only a little more than double the price of one gram, I was figuring on getting the five. Even if I get completely absorbed in using it, according to the formula it would be enough for two hundred liters of sensitizer working solution so it would probably last the rest of my life. Besides, the vendor has a $100 minimum. I'd have no problem with selling you a gram or something when I actually have it.

Or, if you get some first, maybe you can sell me one.

Since even a single gram in a liter of methanol will yield 400 of those 100ml sensitizer solutions, and since the actual cost of the dye per unit ends up being only a few cents, I've been considering the idea of giving it away to holographers who would try it but for the lack of that few cents worth of dye. But, that's a topic for a whole 'nother thread.

Well, putting together kits is one of the things I do for a living now, so that wouldn't be much of a jump. I/we supply small amounts of small things to hobby miniaturists.

You say the dcg-doped litho film made dim holograms, while the emulsion hardness is probably a primary factor, have you by chance measured the emulsion thickness? Somewhere in here recently Dinesh explained that 20 microns is optimum and that too-extreme variations could make a hologram that *looked* dim, but technically may not be (Dinesh, sorry for the oversimplification, but the 20 microns was the essential thing for me to remember). Would a little bit of emulsion swelling make it seem brighter? I can't test that idea here.

Was the film Kodak ortho litho type three? I've got that in 4x5 here, I could measure it.

posts.topic_title: is it just me or is everyone avoiding me

posts.post_subject: is it just me or is everyone avoiding me
posts.content_md:
> i got a very large box 12x18 kodalith type 3

Cool! The 12x18 may have a slightly different emulsion thickness, but it seems to me the type 3 stuff had to be consistent in use regardless of size, so:

Kodak Type 3 Ortho Litho, 4x5 sheet

Mitutoyo digital micrometer, .001mm/.00005", no recent calibration

Starting thickness - ranges from 0.186mm to 0.204mm

After removal of rear coating - 0.185 - 0.188mm

After removal of emulsion (clean film base) - 0.180 - 0.185mm

And Ack! Screwed up and remembered the wrong thing. Dinesh mentioned 20 microns for the early Polygramma emulsion, but says "The "ideal" for emulsion thickness for display is about 10 microns" somewhere in here:

[http://holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewt ... c&start=30](http://holographyforum.org/phpBB2/viewtopic.php?t=2145&postdays=0&postorder=asc&start=30)

Which is good enough for me at this point.

Based on the measurements of the single sheet of film, it seems that the emulsion thickness, at least pre-fixing and re-sensitizing, may be a bit thin at about 5 microns, with a range of maybe +/- 2. How thick is the final hologram?

Now I have to start measuring everything I've got with an emulsion on it.

> also wondering if you can regrow the ag/br crystals in litho film

You mean like developing the film and then rehalogenating? Yeah, but the couple of times I tried that long ago the film didn't end up transparent like holofilm. Someone else may have a usable technique.

Ok, I gathered and abused a number of silver based emulsion products, measured them as best I could, and assembled the results. While I've got some 8E75 on glass plates, I didn't want to waste a plate on mere stripping/measuring. Maybe later. Same with 8x10 sheet film, but I may have a scrap sheet that I can measure.

I'll have to get to the fixing and resensitizing part before I can continue to form an opinion, but based on the info below and elsewhere in this thread is would seem that the Tmax film might be the best choice for doing the DIY with an existing emulsion. Litho looks too thin, some others look too thick but might be good for DCG reworking if they can be softened.

Would such a prehardened emulsion be better for SHSG?

Info on additional existing emulsions may follow.

I can't seem to generate a table in the preview, so I'm condensing the info down to the material info and the apparent emulsion thickness.

Kodak Lantern Plate expired 04/1962 - 0.016mm

Kodak Tmax 100 glass plate, in code - 0.008mm

Applied Holographics wide roll film -0.007mm

Kodak SO-253 High Speed Holographic Film - 0.006mm

4x5 Tri-X Pan (TXT) old, not new, emulsion - 0.014mm

5x7 Tmax 100 - 0.008mm

Kodak Pro Copy Film -0.012mm

Imation RLD imagesetting film - 0.007mm

4x5 Kodalith Type 3 - 0.004mm

VHS Videotape - 0.020mm

Avg'd emulsion thicknesses are a result of averaging the ranges for with & without emulsion and subtracting. If I screwed anything up, well, it's 3am.
